title: How a Dining Hall Learned to Waste Less

paragraphs.en: The entire university dining service wanted to reduce food waste, but its first idea was somewhat vague: encourage everyone to care more. Maybe posters would help, yet the team needed facts before choosing further action. Staff measured the quantity of food left on plates and discovered considerable differences between meal times. A tiny breakfast portion might be enough for one student, while another needed plenty after sports training. Setting an absolute standard for every meal would ignore those differences. The purpose was not to make students feel guilty; it was to understand the condition under which unused food accumulated.
paragraphs.zh: 整个大学餐饮部门想减浪费，首个想法却有些模糊：让大家更在意。海报也许有用，但进一步行动需事实。员工量盘中剩食，发现用餐时段差别很大。运动后有人需要很多，而另一人的极小早餐已足够。给每餐定绝对标准会忽略差异。目的不是让学生内疚，而是理解未食用食物如何累积。

paragraphs.en: A survey of sixty students revealed an array of practical reasons. Some ordered in bulk to avoid returning to the counter, while others selected a large item because no smaller choice was available. The ratio of vegetables to rice also affected appetite. Students sometimes disliked a fragment of unfamiliar seasoning and then discarded a whole dish. Numerous small decisions created an immense total impact. The kitchen had previously focused on the maximum number of meals served, treating waste as a minor factor. This source of information showed that the design of a meal could be as important as the skill of the cook.
paragraphs.zh: 六十名学生调查揭示一系列实际原因：有人一次大量点餐，避免再去柜台，有人因没小份只能选大份。蔬菜米饭比例也影响胃口；有时不喜欢一点陌生调料，就扔整盘。众多小决定造成巨大总影响。厨房原只关注最多供餐量，把浪费当小因素。这信息显示餐食设计可能和厨师技术同样重要。

paragraphs.en: The team tested a different form of service. A tasting spoon gave customers a chance to assess flavor, and a minimum serving could be enlarged at no extra charge. Students remained free to choose a bigger portion, but had to request it rather than receive it automatically. A chunk of waste disappeared immediately, although the initial effect did not guarantee lasting success. Staff paid the utmost attention to food quality, since even an efficient system would fail if customers stopped enjoying the meals. Each change had to make sense in the case of a busy dining hall, where queues already limited time.
paragraphs.zh: 团队试一种不同服务形式：试吃勺让顾客先尝味，最小份可免费加量。学生仍能选大份，但需主动要求，不再自动领。大块浪费立刻减少，不过初效不保证长久成功。员工尽力重视质量，因为即使系统高效，顾客不再爱吃也会失败。每项变化都要适合忙碌食堂，那里排队已挤占时间。

paragraphs.en: The trials also exposed a gap in communication. Menus described ingredients poorly, so students guessed at content and often made a choice they regretted. Clear labels required no tremendous investment but had an undoubtedly useful effect. A new menu included the source of common ingredients and explained which dishes contained allergens. The fact that students could make informed decisions mattered more than promotional claims about sustainability. The team resisted pressure to triple the publicity budget, arguing that a multitude of slogans was less useful than one reliable explanation at the point where people selected their food.
paragraphs.zh: 试验也揭示沟通缺口：菜单食材说明差，学生猜内容，常选后悔。清楚标签无需巨额投入，效果却无疑有用。新菜单列常见食材来源，并说明哪些含过敏原。让学生能知情选择，比宣传可持续更重要。团队拒绝把宣传预算增至三倍，认为大量口号不如选餐处一个可靠解释。

paragraphs.en: After several months, waste had fallen by a meaningful fraction, though innumerable challenges remained. Changing attendance, seasonal produce, and examination schedules all affected demand. The service therefore tracked the magnitude of each change instead of announcing a permanent victory. It kept an ample margin of flexibility in its planning and protected quality as well as cost. The lesson was a practical thing rather than a grand theory: a system improves when people examine its ordinary decisions carefully. Reducing waste began with observation, then turned that observation into choices that made responsible behavior easier for the people using the service.
paragraphs.zh: 数月后浪费减少了可观比例，但挑战仍数不清，出勤变化、季节食材与考试日程均影响需求。部门持续追踪变化大小，不宣布永久胜利；规划留充分灵活余量，同时维护质量与成本。教训很实际，并非宏大理论：认真检查普通决定，系统才改善。减废始于观察，再将观察转成选择，使服务使用者更容易负责行动。
